title: A registry conversation with FamilieSCN2A Foundation

sentences.text: On behalf of CACNA1A Foundation, I invite FamilieSCN2A Foundation to explore a small collaboration for our families.
Published research links both CACNA1A- and SCN2A-related disorders to variants that make proteins do too much or lose function.
The atlas also infers similar symptom patterns, but this connection has confidence 0.47, below 0.5—not confirmation that families’ needs are identical.

sections.heading: What already exists that we could share

sentences.text: Our Contact Registry includes people with CACNA1A-related disorders, while your Dragonfly patient registry includes people with SCN2A-related disorders.
Citizen Health also lists CACNA1A among its communities.
Could we compare registry designs rather than assume that either can serve both communities unchanged?

sections.heading: What must be checked before we join forces

sentences.text: The supplied comparison flags transient unilateral blurring of vision, bradyopsia and 13 more symptoms as not recorded in Dragonfly; please check the full list and whether these first two symptoms also occur in SCN2A-related disorders.
Please also check downbeat nystagmus rather than treating missing records as proof of absence.
The comparison lists neuronal firing and voltage-gated sodium channel activity only on the SCN2A side, whereas CACNA1A is linked to voltage-gated calcium channel activity.
Before proceeding, let’s check the wider CACNA1A organization and research landscape and establish which individual variants increase, impair or remove function.
This month, send FamilieSCN2A Foundation one focused inquiry asking whether Dragonfly could include CACNA1A-related disorders and what changes would need review.
What patient organizations, registries, trials and research groups exist for CACNA1A-related disorders beyond those verified here?
Which individual variants are activating, catalytically impaired or loss of function?
Dear FamilieSCN2A Foundation team,
I’m reaching out on behalf of CACNA1A Foundation to explore learning together.
Published research identifies gain of function in both communities.
Could Dragonfly potentially include CACNA1A-related disorders?
We would welcome an initial discussion of symptom coverage, variant differences and necessary adaptations.
Thank you for considering this conversation.
[Your name], on behalf of CACNA1A Foundation
